title.en: Spot the joke behind the words
title.es: Detectar la broma tras las palabras

es: Reconocer cuándo una frase dice lo contrario de lo que significa (ironía) o resta importancia a un problema grande (understatement).

vocabulary.es: literal, al pie de la letra
atenuación (decir menos de lo que pasa)
en broma, sin hablar en serio

teaching.en: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.
teaching.es: Cuando Tom, empapado hasta los huesos, dice «Qué tiempo tan agradable», su comentario es irónico, porque las palabras contradicen la situación.
teaching.explanationEs: Ironía: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa; el contexto (empapado) delata la intención.
segments: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his
remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.
teaching.audioText: When Tom, soaked to the skin, says “Lovely weather”, his remark is ironic, because the words contradict the situation.

teaching.en: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.es: Quienes quitan importancia a las malas noticias usan la atenuación: una cocina inundada se convierte en «un pequeño desastre».
teaching.explanationEs: Understatement: se dice menos de lo que ocurre; «a bit of a…» es su fórmula más típica.
segments: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a
flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.
teaching.audioText: Speakers who play down bad news use understatement: a flooded kitchen becomes “a bit of a disaster”.

teaching.en: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.
teaching.es: No todo debe tomarse tal cual: «La sopa está caliente» es literal cuando sube vapor del plato.
teaching.explanationEs: Literal: las palabras y la situación coinciden, así que no hay nada oculto.
segments: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is
hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.
teaching.audioText: Not everything should be taken at face value: “The soup is hot” is literal when steam is rising from the bowl.

teaching.en: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.
teaching.es: Lo que quieren decir los hablantes suele esconderse en un tono seco: «Eso no fueron precisamente unas vacaciones» puede describir seis horas de lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: «Not exactly» suaviza un juicio muy negativo; el tono seco lo delata.
segments: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That
was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.
teaching.audioText: What speakers mean is often hidden in a dry tone: “That was not exactly a holiday” can describe six hours of rain.

teaching.en: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.
teaching.es: Para leer entre líneas, pregúntate si las palabras encajan con los hechos; si el fracaso es dolorosamente evidente, el elogio es irónico.
teaching.explanationEs: Método: compara lo dicho con lo ocurrido antes de decidir la intención.
segments: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the
facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.
teaching.audioText: To read between the lines, ask whether the words fit the facts; if the failure is painfully obvious, praise is ironic.

teaching.en: Friends who speak tongue in cheek often keep a straight face, so only the situation shows that they do not mean it.
teaching.es: Los amigos que hablan en broma suelen mantener la cara seria, así que solo la situación muestra que no lo dicen en serio.
teaching.explanationEs: Tongue in cheek: dicho sin seriedad, con una cara que no revela la broma.
segments: Friends who speak tongue in cheek often keep a straight face,
so only the situation shows that they do not mean it.
teaching.audioText: Friends who speak tongue in cheek often keep a straight face, so only the situation shows that they do not mean it.

prompt.es: Mia repara la cadena de la bici: ¿qué quiere decir en realidad con su frase?

choices.text: She enjoyed the repair more than she expected.
She thinks the job was a simple one.
She is annoyed that Leo caused the damage.

feedback.es: El elogio choca con dos horas de trabajo y manos negras de aceite: es ironía y esconde su fastidio con Leo.

hint.es: Compara el elogio con lo que le ha costado a Mia la tarde.

origin.text: Mia has just spent two hours repairing the chain that Leo broke, and her hands are black with oil. She looks at them slowly and says, “Well, that was a great use of my afternoon.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Intentó quitarle importancia al problema.»

answer.text: play down

feedback.es: Play down significa quitar importancia a algo grave; es lo que hace la directora con «a slight inconvenience».

hint.es: Verbo frasal: «jugar» + una dirección hacia abajo.

origin.text: The whole office was flooded on Monday, and the manager wanted to reassure everyone. She tried to ___ the problem by calling it “a slight inconvenience”.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con la idea que transmite.

pairs: a dry tone

pairs.es: voz seca que no revela la broma

pairs: at face value

pairs.es: sin buscar otra intención

pairs: tongue in cheek

pairs.es: dicho sin hablar en serio

pairs: read between the lines

pairs.es: captar lo que no se dice

feedback.es: Las cuatro expresiones describen cómo se dice o cómo se interpreta un comentario, más allá de las palabras literales.

hint.es: Piensa en quién habla y en quién interpreta.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿qué hace el hermano con su respuesta a la recepcionista?

choices.text: He plays down a series of serious problems.
He describes the journey exactly as it happened.
He complains loudly about the airline and the hotel.

feedback.es: Retraso, maleta perdida y habitación cedida son problemas serios; llamarlos «a mixed start» es un understatement.

origin.audio: Our flight was delayed for nine hours, the airline lost my suitcase, and the hotel had given our room to somebody else. When the receptionist asked my brother how the journey had been, he said, with a perfectly straight face, that it had been “a bit of a mixed start”.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿qué actitud deja ver quien lo escribe?

choices.text: Sincere thanks, since the delay allowed a useful chat.
Quiet anger hidden behind exaggerated praise.
Calm acceptance of a delay the writer had expected.
Regret at having ignored the warning.

feedback.es: «Only three hours» y «a great success» suenan a elogio, pero describen un atasco: la queja se esconde tras un agradecimiento exagerado.

origin.text: Thank you for warning us about the traffic. We only spent three hours in the queue, and I am sure the extra time in the car was good for our conversation. The children are still speaking to us, so I suppose the day was a great success.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie tomó sus elogios al pie de la letra.»

answer.text: Nobody took his praise at face value

feedback.es: Take + algo + at face value es la estructura fija para aceptar lo dicho sin cuestionarlo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿qué da a entender la vecina con su comentario sobre el viaje?

choices.text: That she regrets having planned a journey for that week.
That the snow has been only a minor nuisance for the village.
That the situation is serious, but she prefers to treat it lightly.
That she is annoyed with the reporter for arriving so late.

feedback.es: Nueve días aislados hacen de «not exactly the best week» un understatement: la vecina quita importancia a algo grave con humor.

origin.audio: Last winter my village was cut off by snow for nine days. The power failed, the only shop ran out of bread, and the road disappeared under a metre of white. On the third day a reporter arrived on foot and asked my neighbour how everyone was feeling. She sighed, looked at the drifts and said that it had not exactly been the best week for travelling. The reporter wrote it down as if it were a serious remark. The rest of us laughed for an hour, because my neighbour had not left her kitchen since Sunday and had baked forty loaves to feed the street.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende quien escribe este correo a su empleado?

choices.text: To thank the writer for protecting the client's feelings.
To ask the writer politely for a shorter version of the report.
To warn the board that the client was upset by the figures.
To complain about the omissions while seeming to praise them.

feedback.es: Elogia justo lo que no debería haberse hecho (omitir cifras) y cierra con «transparency»: la crítica va envuelta en un elogio irónico.

origin.text: Thanks for your report. I read it on the train and was surprised by how brave you were to leave out every figure that might have upset the client. It is, of course, the kind of omission that makes my job very simple. I shall be sure to tell the board how well you understand our commitment to transparency.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su tono me obligó a leer entre líneas.»

answer.text: lines

feedback.es: Read between the lines es la expresión fija para captar lo que el texto no dice abiertamente; aquí, el enojo de la tía.

origin.text: My aunt wrote that the party had been “a perfect success” and that nobody had “noticed” the burnt cake. She never says what she really thinks, so I had to read between the ___ to understand that she was upset.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada comentario con el tipo que es en su situación.

pairs: “Brilliant service,” said after waiting two hours for a coffee

pairs.es: irónico: dice lo contrario de lo que piensa

pairs: “Brilliant service,” said when the coffee arrives at once

pairs.es: literal: lo dicho coincide con los hechos

pairs: “It is a bit cold,” said while standing in a storm at midnight

pairs.es: atenuación: minimiza un frío terrible

pairs: “Not my finest hour,” said after dropping the wedding cake

pairs.es: atenuación: minimiza un bochorno

feedback.es: Cada frase se clasifica comparando lo dicho con la situación: contradicción, coincidencia o minimización.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor del blog sobre el humor británico?

choices.text: It is indirect rather than unfriendly, and must be interpreted.
It is cold, but visitors are too quick to take offence.
It is best avoided by anyone who cannot read faces.
It is always ironic, so compliments are never sincere.

feedback.es: El autor rechaza que sea «cold»: lo llama «careful» y propone comprobar cada elogio contra los hechos, no descartarlos todos.

origin.text: People tell me that British humour is cold. I would say it is merely careful: we rarely announce our feelings, so a polite “that was interesting” after a terrible dinner can mean almost anything. The key is to watch the face, weigh the situation and never take a compliment at face value until you have checked it against the facts.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo dijo en broma, así que nadie se ofendió.»

answer.text: He said it tongue in cheek, so nobody was offended

feedback.es: Tongue in cheek se coloca tras el verbo y avisa de que no hay intención seria.

prompt.es: Escucha el final del partido: ¿qué pretende el entrenador con su comentario?

choices.text: To praise the creativity of the players sincerely.
To say that the defeat was just bad luck.
To blame the team without saying so directly.

feedback.es: Nueve goles en contra y un tono seco convierten «a great deal of creativity» en una crítica velada, no en un elogio.

origin.audio: After the final whistle, our coach, who had just watched us lose by nine goals, folded his arms and remarked in a dry tone that we had certainly shown a great deal of creativity.

title.es: Juegos de palabras y dobles sentidos

es: Entender cómo funcionan los juegos de palabras basados en homófonos y dobles sentidos y explicar cuál es la palabra clave.

vocabulary.es: depender de, girar en torno a

teaching.en: The banker's pun works because interest means both curiosity and money earned, so he can lose it in two ways.
teaching.es: El juego de palabras del banquero funciona porque interest significa curiosidad y dinero ganado, así que puede perderlo de dos maneras.
teaching.explanationEs: Interest = interés bancario y ganas: una palabra, dos sentidos.
segments: The banker's pun works because interest means both curiosity and
money earned, so he can lose it in two ways.
teaching.audioText: The banker's pun works because interest means both curiosity and money earned, so he can lose it in two ways.

teaching.en: A farmer who wins a prize for being outstanding in his field is a classic case of double meaning.
teaching.es: Un granjero que gana un premio por ser sobresaliente en su campo es un caso clásico de doble sentido.
teaching.explanationEs: Outstanding = excelente y «de pie fuera»; field = campo de cultivo y ámbito profesional.
segments: A farmer who wins a prize for being outstanding in
his field is a classic case of double meaning.
teaching.audioText: A farmer who wins a prize for being outstanding in his field is a classic case of double meaning.

teaching.en: Seafood sounds like see food, a homophone joke that anyone about to go on a diet will recognise.
teaching.es: Seafood suena como see food, un chiste de homófonos que reconocerá cualquiera que esté a punto de ponerse a dieta.
teaching.explanationEs: Homófonos: suenan igual, pero se escriben y significan distinto.
segments: Seafood sounds like see food, a homophone joke that
anyone about to go on a diet will recognise.
teaching.audioText: Seafood sounds like see food, a homophone joke that anyone about to go on a diet will recognise.

teaching.en: A joke about a tailor whose job did not suit him earns a groan, because suit has two senses.
teaching.es: Un chiste sobre un sastre al que el trabajo no le sentaba bien provoca un quejido, porque suit tiene dos sentidos.
teaching.explanationEs: Suit = quedar bien una prenda y convenir un trabajo.
segments: A joke about a tailor whose job did not suit
him earns a groan, because suit has two senses.
teaching.audioText: A joke about a tailor whose job did not suit him earns a groan, because suit has two senses.

teaching.en: The punchline of a pun comes last, and everything before it is preparation that can hinge on one ordinary word.
teaching.es: El remate de un juego de palabras llega al final, y todo lo anterior es una preparación que puede girar en torno a una palabra corriente.
teaching.explanationEs: Hinge on = depender de: sin esa palabra clave, el chiste se cae.
segments: The punchline of a pun comes last, and everything before
it is preparation that can hinge on one ordinary word.
teaching.audioText: The punchline of a pun comes last, and everything before it is preparation that can hinge on one ordinary word.

teaching.en: Wordplay does not survive word for word translation, and a joke that needs explaining will usually fall flat.
teaching.es: El juego de palabras no sobrevive a la traducción palabra por palabra, y un chiste que hay que explicar suele fracasar.
teaching.explanationEs: Fall flat = fracasar: el chiste no provoca la reacción esperada.
segments: Wordplay does not survive word for word translation, and
a joke that needs explaining will usually fall flat.
teaching.audioText: Wordplay does not survive word for word translation, and a joke that needs explaining will usually fall flat.

prompt.es: Lee la escena del panadero y elige los dos sentidos de «dough».

choices.text: A mixture for bread, and an informal word for money.
A mixture for bread, and a kind of oven.
A kind of bread, and a person who lends money.

feedback.es: El panadero no tiene dinero, y dough es la masa del pan y también el dinero en lenguaje informal: de ahí el juego de palabras.

hint.es: Piensa en lo que amasa un panadero y en lo que le falta a alguien que está sin un centavo.

origin.text: The town baker waited outside the bank and sighed. “I am completely broke,” he told the librarian, “and it is not my customers' fault. Everybody says my bread is good, but nobody is giving me any dough.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Un chiste que hay que explicar empieza a fracasar.»

answer.text: flat

feedback.es: Fall flat es la colocación fija para un chiste que no provoca la reacción esperada, sobre todo si se explica.

hint.es: Adjetivo que también describe algo plano y sin relieve.

origin.text: Our teacher told a joke about a bank, but nobody noticed the homophone in the last line. She tried to explain it, and of course the joke began to fall ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El remate depende de una sola palabra corriente.»

answer.text: The punchline hinges on a single ordinary word

feedback.es: Hinge on lleva el verbo en tercera persona (hinges) y la preposición on antes de la palabra clave.

hint.es: El sujeto va primero y on debe ir pegado al verbo.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿qué dos sentidos se mezclan en «a piece of cake»?

choices.text: Something sweet, and something given as a prize.
Something to eat, and something very easy to do.
Something shared at a party, and something left over afterwards.

feedback.es: El alumno se comió la tarea y dice que era «a piece of cake»: un trozo de pastel de verdad y algo facilísimo de hacer.

origin.audio: A friend of mine teaches English, and his favourite joke is about a student who ate his homework. The teacher asked why, and the boy answered that the exercise had been a piece of cake. The class groaned, but the teacher admitted that the joke was not bad.

prompt.es: Lee la anécdota: ¿por qué no funcionó el chiste con la prima?

choices.text: She knew the pun already and found it boring.
She disliked jokes about bicycles and said so.
She heard the wrong word and missed the homophone.
She understood both senses but thought them silly.

feedback.es: La prima entendió «two» como un número de ruedas: no percibió el homófono too, y por eso el remate se quedó sin efecto.

origin.text: When my cousin heard the joke about the bicycle that could not stand up because it was two tired, she asked why two wheels were a problem. I explained that the word was really too, and that the bicycle was also tired. She nodded politely, but the pun had already lost its effect.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La última palabra del chiste lleva los dos sentidos.»

answer.text: The last word of the pun carries both meanings

feedback.es: El sujeto es the last word of the pun; carries both meanings describe su función en el remate.

prompt.es: Escucha al humorista: ¿cómo interpreta el quejido del público?

choices.text: As a mild complaint that audiences make against humour the critics call the lowest form.
As a signal that the preparation took too long for the punchline to surprise anyone.
As an honest reaction that he has learned to accept, although it still hurts a little.
As proof that the listener understood the joke and enjoyed it in spite of himself.

feedback.es: Para el humorista el quejido no es un insulto sino «the highest compliment»: demuestra que el oyente entendió el remate a su pesar.

origin.audio: On the radio last week, a performer explained why he loves puns, even bad ones. A good pun, he said, is a small piece of engineering: the preparation builds one meaning, the punchline switches to another, and the audience has half a second to feel proud. Then comes the groan. He claimed that the groan is not an offence but the highest compliment, because it shows that the listener has understood and cannot forgive himself for enjoying it. Critics say that puns are the lowest form of humour. He smiled and said that they are, but that is exactly why people remember them.

prompt.es: Lee la carta al periódico: ¿qué critica en realidad quien la escribe?

choices.text: The habit of using wordplay instead of informing readers.
The use of any wordplay in a serious newspaper.
The lack of humour in modern headlines.
The decision to give bank news the front page.

feedback.es: El autor acepta el wordplay, pero rechaza que sustituya a la información: su objeción es al hábito, no a los juegos de palabras en sí.

origin.text: Your headline about the bank thief making a run for it might have made me smile if I had not read the same kind of pun three times this month. Headline writers seem to think that any word with two meanings deserves the front page. I do not object to wordplay; I object to wordplay that takes the place of information.

prompt.es: Completa: «El chiste depende de la última palabra.»

answer.text: hinges

feedback.es: Hinges on expresa que todo el efecto depende de un único elemento: aquí, la palabra clave del remate.

origin.text: Nothing in the preparation is funny by itself. The whole joke ___ on the last word, which means one thing in the story and another in the punchline.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada chiste con la palabra clave y sus dos sentidos.

pairs: The clock repairer retired because he had too much time on his hands.

pairs.es: hands: manos del reloj y tiempo libre

pairs: The calendar was worried because its days were numbered.

pairs.es: numbered: con número y a punto de acabar

pairs: The pencil was unhappy because its life had no point.

pairs.es: point: punta y sentido

pairs: The book of problems looked sad: it had so many problems.

pairs.es: problems: ejercicios y preocupaciones

feedback.es: En cada chiste una palabra encaja con dos escenas distintas; encontrarla es explicar el pun.

pairs.es: hands: manos del reloj y tiempo libre

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito defiende los juegos de palabras quien escribe?

choices.text: To persuade pupils to write more jokes of their own.
To show that analysing puns trains useful language skills.
To admit that puns are silly but not dangerous.
To argue that language exercises are useless.

feedback.es: Para ella analizar un pun es «a demanding exercise» que enseña más lengua que marcar casillas: defiende su valor formativo.

origin.text: Some pupils complain that puns are silly. I would argue the opposite: to build a pun, you must hold two meanings in your head at once, and that is a demanding exercise. A pupil who can explain why a joke works has understood more language than one who simply fills in a worksheet.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie se rió, pero el juego de palabras hizo que todos gimieran.»

answer.text: Nobody laughed, but the pun made everyone groan

feedback.es: Make + objeto + verbo base (made everyone groan) expresa que el chiste provoca la reacción.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz: ¿qué le sugiere Leo a Ana?

choices.text: To cut the wordplay from the title because readers may find it too hard.
To explain the pun in a short note printed below the title.
To move the wordplay to the ending so it can surprise readers.
To choose a longer title that contains even more wordplay.

feedback.es: Leo aprecia el pun, pero cree que el título adelanta el final: propone reservarlo para la última línea, donde sorprende.

origin.audio: Hi Ana, it is Leo. I read your draft for the school newspaper. The pun in your title is good, but I think it gives away the ending. Perhaps you could keep the wordplay for the last line, where the punchline can really surprise people.

es: Decidir si un comentario es sincero o sarcástico a partir del contexto, el contraste y las pistas de tono escritas.

teaching.en: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.
teaching.es: Cuando Leo dice «Muchas gracias» con voz plana después de que Ana derrama café sobre sus apuntes, está siendo sarcástico.
teaching.explanationEs: Una voz plana con un contexto negativo es una pista de sarcasmo.
segments: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice
after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.
teaching.audioText: When Leo says “Thanks a lot” in a flat voice after Ana spills coffee on his notes, he is sarcastic.

teaching.en: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.
teaching.es: «Eres tan servicial», dijo Mia con un largo suspiro, y la pista dejó claro a todos que el elogio no era sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: El suspiro es una pista: el elogio suena falso.
segments: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and
the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.
teaching.audioText: “You are so helpful,” said Mia with a long sigh, and the cue told everyone that the praise was not sincere.

teaching.en: There is often a contrast between happy words and a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.
teaching.es: A menudo hay un contraste entre palabras alegres y una cara cansada, y ese contraste marca claramente el sarcasmo.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraste entre palabras y gesto delata el sarcasmo.
segments: There is often a contrast between happy words and
a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.
teaching.audioText: There is often a contrast between happy words and a tired face, and that contrast clearly marks sarcasm.

teaching.en: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.es: Fue una reunión tan larga que Tom soltó un suspiro de alivio cuando terminó.
teaching.explanationEs: Such a + adjetivo + nombre intensifica; después, that introduce el resultado.
segments: It was such a long meeting that Tom let
out a sigh of relief when it ended.
teaching.audioText: It was such a long meeting that Tom let out a sigh of relief when it ended.

teaching.en: “Your cooking is surprisingly good” is a backhanded compliment, and its sarcastic edge is thinly disguised.
teaching.es: «Tu cocina es sorprendentemente buena» es un cumplido con doble filo, y su punta sarcástica apenas está disimulada.
teaching.explanationEs: Un elogio que esconde una crítica: «surprisingly» revela que esperaba lo contrario.
segments: “Your cooking is surprisingly good” is a backhanded
compliment, and its sarcastic edge is thinly disguised.
teaching.audioText: “Your cooking is surprisingly good” is a backhanded compliment, and its sarcastic edge is thinly disguised.

teaching.en: A flat voice can give the game away even when the words are polite, so always listen for the cue.
teaching.es: Una voz plana puede delatar la intención aunque las palabras sean corteses, así que escucha siempre la pista.
teaching.explanationEs: Give the game away: dejar al descubierto lo que alguien quería ocultar.
segments: A flat voice can give the game away even when
the words are polite, so always listen for the cue.
teaching.audioText: A flat voice can give the game away even when the words are polite, so always listen for the cue.

prompt.es: Lee la escena: ¿qué pista delata que Carlos no es sincero?

choices.text: The schedule was new, so he is confused.
His flat voice and sigh contradict his words.
His words are positive, so they are sincere.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que todo está claro, pero el suspiro y la voz plana van en sentido contrario: el tono delata el sarcasmo.

hint.es: Mira qué hacen su voz y su cuerpo mientras habla.

origin.text: After Sara had explained the new schedule for the third time, Carlos sighed, looked at the ceiling and said in a flat voice, “Oh, that is so clear now.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue un viaje tan largo que todos nos dormimos.»

answer.text: such

feedback.es: Con un nombre (journey) detrás del adjetivo se usa such a; so solo acompañaría a un adjetivo suelto.

hint.es: Después del espacio vienen a + adjetivo + nombre.

origin.text: The train was delayed twice, and then it stopped for an hour in an empty field. It was ___ a long journey that we all fell asleep.

feedback.es: Las cuatro son pistas de sarcasmo: dos de tono, una de contexto y una de contenido.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena: ¿qué quiere decir Mia con «you are so reliable»?

choices.text: That Leo has done well and deserves thanks.
That Leo is reliable, although he forgot one thing.
That Leo is not reliable, and she is annoyed.

feedback.es: El suspiro y las manos vacías contradicen el elogio: Mia usa «reliable» con sarcasmo para reprochar el olvido.

origin.audio: Leo had promised to bring the tickets for the concert, but he arrived at the station with empty hands. Mia looked at him, gave a long sigh and said, “Well, you are so reliable.” Everybody laughed except Leo, who stared at the floor.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento: ¿qué hace sarcástico el segundo comentario de Sara?

choices.text: She repeats the word plan in both remarks.
She speaks while she is busy with her phone.
She uses a longer sentence than in her first remark.
The praise comes just after she finds the Sunday meetings.

feedback.es: El contexto decide: felicita a Carlos justo cuando descubre reuniones en domingo, así que el elogio es una crítica disfrazada.

origin.text: Carlos handed Sara the new schedule. “It is such a lovely plan,” said Sara, without looking up from her phone. Then she put the phone down, turned the page, found the same meetings on Sunday, and added, “Really, you have thought of everything.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una reunión tan larga que todos suspiraron.»

answer.text: It was such a long meeting that everybody sighed

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre va seguido de that + resultado: la estructura intensifica y explica la consecuencia.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato: ¿cómo responde la jefa al comentario de Carlos?

choices.text: She has understood the sarcasm and answers it with a polite challenge.
She takes his remark as a genuine compliment and rewards him with a new task.
She feels hurt by his comment and brings the meeting to an end at once.
She accepts that the rota needs more work and thanks him for his honesty.

feedback.es: Sonríe y le pide que organice el siguiente: es un desafío cortés que muestra que captó el sarcasmo, y Carlos lo entiende así.

origin.audio: Our manager presented the new weekend rota for the third time, and each time it had changed. When she finished, my colleague Carlos put his hand up and said, in a perfectly flat voice, that he had rarely seen such a well organised plan. Nobody spoke. The manager smiled, thanked him warmly and asked whether he would like to help organise the next one. Carlos went pale and said that, on reflection, the plan was not so bad. Afterwards Sara whispered that she respected his courage, because sarcasm is always a risk when the listener is also the boss.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura de quien escribe sobre el sarcasmo con su hijo adolescente?

choices.text: It is dangerous, so she should never use it with young people.
It is acceptable when the son can answer back in the same way.
It is better than a lecture in every family conversation she has.
It is a habit that she has copied from her own sixteen-year-old son.

feedback.es: No lo rechaza ni lo defiende sin más: lo acepta mientras el hijo pueda responder igual, porque solo duele cuando no hay réplica.

origin.text: I am told that I should not use sarcasm with my sixteen-year-old son. Perhaps so. But when he says that cleaning his room is a lovely chance, he is hardly sincere himself, and I find a dry reply more honest than a lecture. Sarcasm only hurts when the listener has no chance to answer in kind.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue un cumplido envenenado, cortés por fuera e hiriente por dentro.»

answer.text: backhanded

feedback.es: Backhanded compliment es la colocación para un elogio que contiene una crítica: amable en apariencia, hiriente en el fondo.

origin.text: When Sara won the prize, her opponent said, “Congratulations, you must be surprised that the judges chose you.” It was a ___ compliment, polite on the surface and rude inside.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la abuela con su comentario sobre el traje?

choices.text: That she respects his courage in choosing the colour.
That he will be easy to find if he gets lost.
That the suit is too loud, though she avoids saying so.
That she would prefer him to buy a different suit.

feedback.es: La abuela nunca critica de frente: «nobody will lose you» es un cumplido con doble filo, y el resto de la familia capta el tono.

origin.text: My grandmother never says anything rude. When my cousin arrived in a bright orange suit, she looked him up and down and said, “Well, nobody will lose you in a crowd.” He took it as a compliment. The rest of the family, who know her tone, did not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Nadie le creyó, porque su voz plana lo delató.»

answer.text: Nobody believed him because his flat voice gave the game away

feedback.es: Give the game away lleva el objeto en medio: gave the game away, con la causa introducida por because.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota: ¿por qué entiende el camarero la queja al instante?

choices.text: Because the uncle had complained about the same soup several times before.
Because the uncle asked him openly to change the soup.
Because the waiter had already noticed that the soup was cold.
Because what the uncle said clashed with what was plainly on the table.

feedback.es: Elogiar una «warm welcome» ante un plato frío es un contraste evidente: el camarero capta la queja sin que se formule.

origin.audio: When the waiter asked how the soup was, my uncle looked at the cold bowl, sighed and said that it was such a warm welcome. The waiter understood at once and offered to heat it up, because the contrast between the words and the bowl was painfully clear.

es: Escribir una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such… that, un correlativo y suavizadores que mantengan el buen tono.

teaching.en: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.
teaching.es: La hipérbole es exageración a propósito: «Llevo esperando cien años» convierte una demora corta en una broma.
teaching.explanationEs: Nadie lo toma al pie de la letra: por eso hace reír en vez de mentir.
segments: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for
a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.
teaching.audioText: Hyperbole is exaggeration on purpose: “I have been waiting for a hundred years” turns a short delay into a joke.

teaching.en: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.
teaching.es: Cuando los amigos exageran una queja en broma, como «Este café es tan flojo que casi es agua», todos entienden el juego.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo + that + resultado absurdo: la estructura típica de la queja exagerada.
segments: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is
so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.
teaching.audioText: When friends exaggerate a mock complaint, such as “This coffee is so weak that it is practically water”, everybody understands the game.

teaching.en: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.
teaching.es: Un suavizador como kind of o only joking mantiene amistosa una exageración, porque muestra que no se quiere hacer daño.
teaching.explanationEs: Los suavizadores avisan del tono: sin ellos, una broma puede sonar a ataque.
segments: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an
exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.
teaching.audioText: A softener such as kind of or only joking keeps an exaggeration friendly, because it shows that no harm is meant.

teaching.en: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.
teaching.es: Tanto la queja como la respuesta son exageradas, pero ambos autores siguen siendo corteses y quitan filo al momento.
teaching.explanationEs: Both… and une dos elementos; el verbo va en plural.
segments: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both
writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.
teaching.audioText: Both the complaint and the reply are exaggerated, yet both writers stay polite and take the edge off the moment.

teaching.en: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can go too far; neither result is pure luck.
teaching.es: O una broma hace sonreír a todos, o puede pasarse de la raya; ninguno de los dos resultados es pura suerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Either… or ofrece dos opciones; neither… nor las descarta, con el verbo en afirmativo.
segments: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can
go too far; neither result is pure luck.
teaching.audioText: Either a joke makes everyone smile, or it can go too far; neither result is pure luck.

teaching.en: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.
teaching.es: Una hipérbole como «el peor día de la historia» es desproporcionada para un autobús que llega tarde, y ese desfase la hace graciosa.
teaching.explanationEs: Out of proportion: la distancia entre lo dicho y lo ocurrido es el motor de la broma.
segments: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of
proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.
teaching.audioText: Hyperbole such as “the worst day in history” is out of proportion to a late bus, and that gap makes it funny.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Tom: ¿cuál es la hipérbole?

choices.text: honestly, it was kind of a disaster
but I am only joking about the whole thing
so long that I could have written a novel

feedback.es: La hipérbole es el resultado absurdo con so… that; kind of y only joking son los suavizadores que rebajan el tono.

hint.es: Busca la parte que nadie podría creer al pie de la letra.

origin.text: Tom sent his friend a message after the concert: “The queue was so long that I could have written a novel. Honestly, it was kind of a disaster, but I am only joking.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Ni mi hermano ni mi hermana probaron un trozo.»

answer.text: nor

feedback.es: Neither se completa siempre con nor, nunca con or: los dos elementos quedan descartados.

hint.es: Es la pareja negativa de neither.

origin.text: The pizza was so small that I could have eaten it in one bite, and neither my brother ___ my sister got a single slice.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Fue una cola tan larga que aprendí italiano.»

answer.text: It was such a long queue that I learned Italian

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + nombre va seguido de that + resultado absurdo: la hipérbole queda completa.

hint.es: Such a va antes del adjetivo y del nombre; that introduce el resultado.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje: ¿qué hace la hablante con «the driver is on holiday»?

choices.text: She exaggerates to be funny and then softens the remark.
She reports a rumour that she has heard from other passengers.
She makes a serious accusation and then regrets it at once.

feedback.es: Nadie cree que el conductor esté de vacaciones: es una hipérbole cómica que «only joking» suaviza inmediatamente.

origin.audio: I have been standing at this bus stop for so long that the birds know me by name. The timetable promises a bus every ten minutes, but I am almost certain that the driver is on holiday. Only joking, of course. I am sure that he will arrive soon, and I will forgive him at once.

prompt.es: Lee la respuesta a Tom: ¿por qué podría resultar ofensiva?

choices.text: It mocks Tom's own effort, and the softener comes too late.
It exaggerates so much that nobody could possibly believe a single word.
It contains no softener at all, so it sounds sincere.
It praises the pasta in a way that sounds false.

feedback.es: La broma apunta al esfuerzo del anfitrión y el suavizador final llega después del golpe: no consigue quitar el filo.

origin.text: Dear Tom, your pasta was so heavy that the table needed a rest, and you clearly believe that cooking is either an art or a test for your guests. No offence, of course.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tanto mi teléfono como mi paraguas dejaron de funcionar.»

answer.text: Both my phone and my umbrella stopped working

feedback.es: Both… and une los dos sujetos y el verbo queda en plural: stopped working.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario radiofónico: ¿por qué funciona la exageración de la columnista?

choices.text: It hides her real opinion of the train behind jokes she does not mean.
It expresses genuine tiredness without turning the complaint bitter.
It shows that commuters on her train really do swap birthdays.
It follows a rule from her editor that every column must contain a joke.

feedback.es: La exageración expresa un cansancio real sin volver amarga la queja: los chistes la suavizan y la regla del editor limita el daño.

origin.audio: In her column about public transport, the writer complains that her morning train is so crowded that she has learned to sleep standing up, that the train is such a tiny space that commuters exchange birthdays by the third stop, and that neither the conductor nor the timetable has ever told the truth. Readers love it, because nobody believes a word of it. The exaggeration is her way of saying that she is tired, and the jokes soften a complaint that might otherwise sound bitter. Her editor adds only one rule: never go too far, and never aim the joke at a person who could be hurt.

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca con la broma del comienzo quien responde a Sara?

choices.text: To turn the complaint into a joke so that it can be forgotten quickly.
To share the blame with the kitchen staff in a friendly way.
To keep the mood friendly while still taking the complaint seriously.
To avoid offering a solution by making the whole matter a joke.

feedback.es: La broma exagera el problema para acercarse a Sara, y el almuerzo gratis y el cierre serio demuestran que la queja sí se toma en serio.

origin.text: Dear Sara, I am sorry that your sandwich was cold. It was such a dramatic disaster that I have asked the kitchen to hold a minute of silence. Only joking: I have already arranged a free lunch for you, and I hope that this small gesture shows how seriously we take every complaint.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una sonrisa y un «solo bromeaba» pueden quitar filo a una queja.»

answer.text: take

feedback.es: Take the edge off es la expresión fija para suavizar algo que resultaba demasiado duro.

origin.text: A quick smile and an “only joking” can ___ the edge off a sharp complaint. Without them, even a friendly exaggeration might sound like an attack.

prompt.es: Escribe una queja exagerada y la respuesta bromista de un amigo (180–240 palabras).

answer.text: My complaint is simple: the queue at the post office was so long that I learned to play the guitar while I waited. It was such a slow morning that the clocks went on strike, and both my patience and my shoes were worn out before I reached the window. Either the post office has forgotten how to count, or the staff are training to become statues. I am kind of upset, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered at once: Poor you! You are so dramatic that the theatre should call you. Neither the queue nor the clerk deserves such an unfair review, but either you take a book next time, or I will bring you a chair. Only joking: come to my house, and I will make you a hot chocolate.
accepted: My complaint is simple: the queue at the post office was so long that I learned to play the guitar while I waited. It was such a slow morning that the clocks went on strike, and both my patience and my shoes were worn out before I reached the window. Either the post office has forgotten how to count, or the staff are training to become statues. I am kind of upset, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered at once: Poor you! You are so dramatic that the theatre should call you. Neither the queue nor the clerk deserves such an unfair review, but either you take a book next time, or I will bring you a chair. Only joking: come to my house, and I will make you a hot chocolate.

Here is my complaint about the bus. The journey was so slow that I finished a whole novel, and the seat was such a hard seat that I now walk like a robot. Both my phone and my umbrella stopped working, and neither the driver nor the weather said sorry. Either the bus company has lost the map, or the driver is taking the scenic route around the planet. I am sort of tired, but I am just joking. My friend Mia replied: Poor you! You are so brave that you deserve a medal. Either you leave earlier, or I will buy you a bicycle. Only kidding. Come for dinner tonight, and I will cook pasta, so we can complain about the bus together.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa exagera con so… that y such a…, reparte la queja con un correlativo y mantiene el buen tono con un suavizador.

origin.text: Escribe en inglés una queja exagerada sobre algo cotidiano (una cola, un atasco, un autobús) y la respuesta bromista de un amigo. Usa dos estructuras de intensidad (so… that y such a…), un correlativo (both… and, either… or o neither… nor) y un suavizador (kind of, only joking).

prompt.es: ¿Qué postura defiende el autor del blog sobre la exageración?

choices.text: It is a form of lying that speakers should avoid.
It is acceptable in every situation, between any two people.
It is acceptable whenever the speaker says that he is only joking.
It is acceptable when both sides know that it is not literal.

feedback.es: Antes la veía como mentira; ahora la entiende como un pacto: es aceptable mientras ambos saben que no es literal y el tema no hiere.

origin.text: I used to think that exaggeration was a form of lying. Now I see that it is a kind of contract: the speaker promises not to be taken literally, and the listener promises to laugh. The contract breaks only when the joke is about something that the other person cannot change, because then nobody is playing a game any more.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ni el autobús ni el clima tuvieron la culpa.»

answer.text: Neither the bus nor the weather was to blame

feedback.es: Neither… nor concuerda con el sujeto más cercano (the weather) y el verbo va en afirmativo: was.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de mi hermano: ¿qué queja es real y no una exageración?

choices.text: The length of the film he watched.
The price of the ice cream he bought.
The low temperature inside the cinema.

feedback.es: El helado congelado y los créditos eternos son hipérboles; el «kind of serious» revela que lo que de verdad le molestó fue el frío.

origin.audio: My brother sent me a complaint about the cinema. He said that the room was so cold that the ice cream froze, and that the film was so long that the credits felt like a holiday. Then he added that he was kind of serious about the cold, because he had to borrow a stranger's coat. I replied that he should bring one next time.

title.en: A funny toast for a friend
title.es: Un brindis gracioso para un amigo

es: Preparar un brindis de cumpleaños con bromas amables, una hipérbole con so/such y una revisión que elimina lo ofensivo.

teaching.en: A good toast opens with a generous word, so every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.
teaching.es: Un buen brindis empieza con una palabra generosa, así que cada broma que sigue se siente como amistad y no como ataque.
teaching.explanationEs: Empieza por lo cálido: el humor posterior se interpreta con ese tono.
segments: A good toast opens with a generous word, so
every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.
teaching.audioText: A good toast opens with a generous word, so every joke that follows feels like friendship, not attack.

teaching.en: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.
teaching.es: Las bromas suaves sobre pequeños hábitos, como llegar tarde a su propia fiesta, hacen cálido un discurso y no grosero.
teaching.explanationEs: Bromea sobre hábitos inocentes que la persona pueda cambiar y reírse de ellos.
segments: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to
her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.
teaching.audioText: Gentle teasing about small habits, such as arriving late to her own party, makes a speech warm, not rude.

teaching.en: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.
teaching.es: Las bromas sobre la edad, el dinero o el aspecto son ofensivas, y una anécdota embarazosa puede dejar en silencio a toda la sala.
teaching.explanationEs: Temas prohibidos: edad, dinero, aspecto y cualquier cosa que avergüence.
segments: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an
embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.
teaching.audioText: Jokes about age, money or looks are offensive, and an embarrassing story can make the whole room go silent.

teaching.en: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke might cross the line between teasing and being rude.
teaching.es: Cuando revises un borrador, pregúntate si alguna broma podría pasarse de la raya entre bromear y ser grosero.
teaching.explanationEs: Revisar es parte del brindis: la línea entre cariño y ofensa es fina.
segments: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke
might cross the line between teasing and being rude.
teaching.audioText: When you revise a draft, ask whether any joke might cross the line between teasing and being rude.

teaching.en: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.
teaching.es: Si un comentario parece peligroso, suaviza la exageración, conserva el cariño y termina el discurso con un sincero cheers.
teaching.explanationEs: Tone down: bajar la intensidad sin perder la intención amable.
segments: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep
the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.
teaching.audioText: If a remark feels dangerous, tone down the exaggeration, keep the kindness and finish the speech with a sincere cheers.

teaching.en: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.
teaching.es: Un brindis debe ser bien recibido por todos, así que invita a los invitados a alzar la copa solo tras la última palabra amable.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre sincero y el gesto de brindar rematan el discurso.
segments: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the
guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.
teaching.audioText: A toast should go down well with everybody, so invite the guests to raise a glass only after the last kind word.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador de Leo: ¿qué broma debería quitar?

choices.text: The joke about Tom's age.
The joke about the wedding cake.
The joke about the coffee.

feedback.es: Las bromas sobre hábitos (tarde, generoso) son cariñosas; la de la edad es el tema que más fácilmente ofende y conviene cortarla.

hint.es: Piensa en qué rasgo no puede cambiar Tom.

origin.text: Leo's draft for Tom's birthday has three jokes. First: Tom is so late that he arrived at his own wedding after the cake. Second: Tom is so old that his birthday candles need a fire permit. Third: Tom is so generous that he pays for everybody's coffee.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una broma sobre su edad se pasaría de la raya.»

answer.text: cross

feedback.es: Cross the line es la expresión fija para pasarse del límite entre la broma cariñosa y la ofensiva.

hint.es: Verbo que significa atravesar un límite.

origin.text: Mia loves jokes about her terrible map-reading, but a joke about her age would ___ the line. Her brother knows exactly where it is.

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué broma le pide su hermano que quite del brindis?

choices.text: The joke about how dangerous his cooking is.
The joke about how much money he makes.
The joke about losing his own birthday.

feedback.es: Se ríe de las bromas sobre su memoria y su cocina, pero pide que quite la del sueldo: es un tema personal que prefiere dejar fuera.

origin.audio: Mia read her draft toast to her brother. She had written that he was so forgetful that he once lost his own birthday, and that his cooking was such a danger to the neighbourhood that the firefighters knew his name. Her brother laughed, but he asked her to remove the line about his salary.

prompt.es: Lee la nota de la invitada: ¿qué opina del discurso?

choices.text: It was almost perfect, but too many jokes were about habits.
Part of it made some guests laugh but hurt another.
It was a success with all, including the grandmother.
It was almost perfect, but the grandmother should have laughed too.

feedback.es: Elogia el discurso («almost perfect»), pero señala que la broma sobre la edad hizo reír a los amigos y dejó incómoda a la abuela.

origin.text: Thanks for the speech, it was almost perfect. The joke about Tom's age got a big laugh from his friends, but his grandmother looked at her plate for the rest of the evening. Next time, perhaps we could keep the teasing for things that he can change.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Suaviza cualquier broma que pueda avergonzar al invitado.»

answer.text: Tone down any joke that might be embarrassing for the guest

feedback.es: Tone down lleva después el objeto (any joke) y una oración relativa que explica el riesgo.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato de la boda: ¿qué se deduce del silencio y de la reacción de la madre?

choices.text: That his mother disliked the earlier jokes as well as the last one.
That the speech ran long and the guests lost interest before the end.
That the line about the first wife crossed the line for the family.
That the best man had meant to upset the family on purpose.

feedback.es: Las bromas de hábitos funcionaron, pero la mención de la antigua novia provocó silencio y el gesto de la madre: esa línea fue la que se pasó de la raya.

origin.audio: At my cousin's wedding, the best man stood up with a card in one hand and a glass in the other. He began well: he said that my cousin was so generous that he had once given away his only umbrella in a storm, and so late for everything that his own wife had learned to tell him the wedding started an hour earlier. The guests laughed. Then he mentioned my cousin's first wife, and the room went quiet. My cousin's smile did not move, but his mother put down her glass. Afterwards the best man admitted that he had not read the room, and that one line had changed the whole evening.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le aconseja a Leo quien escribe el correo sobre su borrador?

choices.text: To delete the whole second page because it is too long for a toast.
To keep every joke, since Sara laughs at everything about herself.
To replace the cake joke with a more generous comment.
To keep the habit jokes and soften or cut the dress line.

feedback.es: Aprueba la broma del pastel porque Sara se ríe de ella, pero recomienda suavizar o eliminar la del vestido, que afecta algo que eligió con cuidado.

origin.text: Dear Leo, I have read your toast twice. The first page is lovely: the joke about Sara arriving after the cake is exactly the right kind of teasing, because she laughs at it herself. The second page worries me. The line about her dress might be funny to you, but I would tone it down, or leave it out, because she chose that dress with great care.

prompt.es: Completa: «Pidió a todos que alzaran una copa por la feliz pareja.»

answer.text: raise

feedback.es: Raise a glass es la expresión habitual para invitar a brindar al final de un discurso.

origin.text: After the last joke, the best man thanked the guests for their patience. Then he asked everybody to ___ a glass to the happy couple.

prompt.es: Escribe el brindis para Mia con bromas amables y una revisión (200–260 palabras).

answer.text: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Mia, who turns thirty today! Mia is so generous that she cooks dinner for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. She is kind of famous for her terrible maps, but she is such a good friend that we always follow her anyway. I had planned a joke about her age, but I have decided to cut it, because it could be embarrassing for her and it would not be fair. Instead, I want to say something sincere: thank you, Mia, for being the first person to call when things go wrong, and the last one to leave when they go right. We are lucky to have you. Cheers, Mia, and happy birthday!
accepted: Friends and family, please raise a glass to Mia, who turns thirty today! Mia is so generous that she cooks dinner for the whole street, and she is so late for everything that she arrived at her own party after the cake. I am only joking: we would wait for her all night. She is kind of famous for her terrible maps, but she is such a good friend that we always follow her anyway. I had planned a joke about her age, but I have decided to cut it, because it could be embarrassing for her and it would not be fair. Instead, I want to say something sincere: thank you, Mia, for being the first person to call when things go wrong, and the last one to leave when they go right. We are lucky to have you. Cheers, Mia, and happy birthday!

Dear friends, let us all raise a glass to Carlos on his fortieth birthday. He is so kind that he lends his car to anybody who asks, and he is so forgetful that he once looked for his phone while he was talking on it. I am just joking: we love him exactly as he is. Carlos is sort of a legend in the kitchen, but he is such a funny cook that we always eat before we arrive. I wrote a joke about his money, and I will not read it, because it would be unfair and it could hurt people who love him. Thank you, Carlos, for every good day, and for always being the first person to help when something goes wrong. Cheers to Carlos, and happy birthday!

feedback.es: Un brindis completo tiene bromas amables con so/such… that, un suavizador, la revisión visible de lo que se retira y un cierre sincero.

origin.text: Mia cumple 30 años. Es muy generosa, siempre llega tarde y se pierde con los mapas. Escribe en inglés un brindis: dos bromas amables con so/such… that, un suavizador (kind of, only joking), una broma sobre su edad que decides quitar y un cierre sincero con cheers.

evidenceGroups: i will not make a joke
i would not make a joke

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe esta columna quien firma el texto?

choices.text: To persuade speakers to cut any joke that they are unsure about.
To suggest that speakers should always read their jokes to their mothers.
To explain how to write the funniest lines for a speech.
To ban all jokes in speeches given at family parties.

feedback.es: Su regla es práctica: ante la duda, corta; el criterio de «repetirlo ante su madre» sirve para decidir, no prohíbe el humor.

origin.text: Nobody has ever been sorry that they cut a dangerous joke. Many have been sorry that they kept one. When in doubt, ask yourself whether the person being teased would repeat the line to her mother. If not, it probably does not belong in the speech, however well it sounds in your head.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por favor, alza la copa por mi generoso amigo.»

answer.text: Please raise a glass to my generous friend

feedback.es: Raise a glass to + persona es la fórmula para invitar al brindis; el adjetivo generous va antes del nombre.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia: ¿qué actitud muestra ante el brindis de Leo?

choices.text: She is happy with the whole speech and says he should repeat it exactly.
She is pleased overall but asks him to cut the joke that embarrassed others.
She is upset by the age joke and will only forgive him after an apology.
She agrees with her aunt that the joke about the maps went too far.

feedback.es: Celebra la broma sobre los mapas, pero pide quitar la de su edad, que incomodó a otros: aprueba el tono general y corrige un punto.

origin.audio: Hi Leo, it is Mia. I listened to the recording of your toast. The part about my terrible maps made everybody laugh, and I loved it. The part about my age, on the other hand, made my aunt stare at her plate. Please leave that one out next time, and I will forgive you completely.
